title: Reading a bar graph and finding the mode

pedagogy.rationale: Learners read one class data set from a table, then a bar graph, then answer questions that need the graph, ending with the mode.

prerequisiteAssumptions: Learners can count and compare whole numbers to 50.
Scope: this lesson covers bar graphs and the mode; line graphs, pie charts, mean and median are taught in later lessons of the same objective.

misconceptions.description: Thinks the mode is the largest count rather than the category with the largest count.
misconceptions.response: The mode is the answer chosen most often (mango), not the number 9.

misconceptions.description: Compares bars by width or position instead of height.
misconceptions.response: Read where the top of each bar meets the number scale.

scenes.title: Class 4's favourite fruit
scenes.learnerAction: Guess which fruit your own class would choose most.

content.body:
Class 4 voted for their favourite fruit on anonymous slips: no names were written, and anyone could choose not to vote. The counts (illustrative) were: mango 9, banana 6, orange 4, pineapple 3.

How can we show these numbers so anyone can read them quickly?

accessibility.textAlternative: Anonymous fruit votes in Class 4: mango 9, banana 6, orange 4, pineapple 3.

scenes.title: What you will be able to do

content.body: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
keyPoints: Read the values shown by a bar graph.
Answer questions using a bar graph.
Find the mode of a data set.

accessibility.textAlternative: Goal: read a bar graph, answer questions with it, and find the mode.

scenes.title: The bar graph
scenes.learnerAction: Read the height of each bar against the number scale.

content.body:
A bar graph has a bar for each fruit. The **height** of each bar shows how many votes it got: read where the top of the bar meets the number scale on the side.

The mango bar reaches 9, banana 6, orange 4 and pineapple 3.

media.description: Vertical bar graph titled Favourite fruit in Class 4: bars for mango (9), banana (6), orange (4), pineapple (3) against a scale from 0 to 10.
media.altText: Bar graph of favourite fruit: mango 9, banana 6, orange 4, pineapple 3. Mango has the tallest bar.

fallback.content: Draw the graph on squared paper: a scale from 0 to 10 up the side, and a bar for each fruit: mango up to 9, banana up to 6, orange up to 4, pineapple up to 3.

hints: Follow the top of the bar across to the scale.

accessibility.textAlternative: Bar graph of favourite fruit: mango 9 votes, banana 6, orange 4, pineapple 3. The bar heights show the counts; mango is tallest.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Read the text description, then Continue.

offline.note: The graph image must be cached; the squared-paper drawing works without it.

scenes.title: Match each fruit to its count
scenes.learnerAction: Match each fruit to the number its bar shows.

content.body: Use the bar graph to match each fruit to its number of votes.

interaction.prompt: Match each fruit to its number of votes.

fallback.content: Write each fruit and the number its bar shows, for example: mango - 9.

hints: Read the top of each bar.

accessibility.textAlternative: Match mango, banana, orange and pineapple to 9, 6, 4 and 3 using the bar graph.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Choose each fruit with Tab, then its number from a list.
accessibility.nonPointerAlternative: Pick each fruit's count from a list with the keyboard instead of drawing lines.

scenes.title: Finding the mode
scenes.learnerAction: Follow the example and say the mode aloud.

content.body:
The **mode** is the value that appears most often. In a bar graph it is the category with the tallest bar.

The tallest bar is mango, with 9 votes. So the mode is **mango**, not 9: the mode is the answer people chose most.

accessibility.textAlternative: The mode is the most common answer. The tallest bar is mango with 9 votes, so the mode is mango.

scenes.title: Quick check
scenes.learnerAction: Choose an answer for each question.

content.body: Use the fruit bar graph to answer.

items.prompt: How many more votes did banana get than orange?

options.feedback: That adds the two bars. How many more means subtract.
4 is the orange bar itself. Compare banana (6) with orange (4).

items.prompt: What is the mode of the fruit votes?

options.feedback: 9 is the count. The mode is the fruit with that count.
Yes. Mango has the tallest bar, so it is the mode.
Pineapple has the shortest bar: the fewest votes.

hints: Read each bar's top against the scale.

accessibility.textAlternative: Two questions using the fruit votes: how many more chose banana than orange, and what the mode is.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

content.body: Write a short answer in your own words.

prompts.prompt: Why is a bar graph easier to read than a list of votes?

accessibility.textAlternative: Write why a bar graph is easier to read than a list of votes.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to the text box and type.

content.body: Answer each question. Your answers are checked by the school's learning system, not on this device.

accessibility.textAlternative: Final questions reading a bar graph and finding a mode, with every graph described in text.
accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab to each option and press Space.

fallback.content: Your teacher draws the graph on the board and records your answers on paper.
